comparison: Perfect agreement on phylogenetic classification and expression data (C6, C39-C41). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED without concerns.

Partial disagreement on biochemical characterization (C7, C42-C61). OpenEval finds all claims SUPPORTED including cellulose product validation. Peer review accepts catalytic activity data but rates UNCERTAIN due to insufficient product characterization - specifically requesting additional methods beyond cellulase digestion (linkage analysis, TEM of microfibrils).
Complete agreement on cryo-EM structural data (C8, C63-C70). Both evaluations find the structures well-resolved and SUPPORTED, with comprehensive comparison to prior structures.

Agreement on TM7 repositioning and lipid-exposed channel (C73-C78). Both find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review accepts the structural observation but notes lack of explanation for differences between primary and secondary cell wall CesAs.
Agreement on NTD conformational flexibility (C80-C83). Both evaluations find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review notes this provides limited new functional insight despite being structurally valid.
Agreement on CSR disorder and partial resolution (C84-C88). Both evaluations find evidence SUPPORTED and consistent with prior predictions of intrinsic disorder.

Complete agreement on isoform-specific interactions (C10, C12, C90-C94). Both evaluations find the tandem affinity purification data SUPPORTED, including interactions between different isoforms and appropriate negative controls.

Agreement on NTD deletion experiments (C95-C96). Both evaluations find SUPPORTED that NTD is not required for trimerization or interactions. OpenEval also covers CSR deletion data (C13, C98-C100) not explicitly mentioned in this peer result.

Agreement on CSR requirement for interactions (C13, C98-C100). Both evaluations find SUPPORTED that CSR mediates inter-isoform contacts. OpenEval also includes NTD deletion data (C95-C96) in same result.

Disagreement on clustering observations (C15, C101-C109). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED for clustering and upside-down arrangements. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, expressing skepticism about biological relevance and noting aggregates don't form expected rosette/hexameric structures.

Agreement on synergistic activity (C11, C110-C113). Both evaluations find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review notes 2-fold synergy is 'not dramatic' and mechanism unclear, but accepts the data as interesting and valid.

Complete agreement on inactive trimer experiments (C114-C115, C117-C118). Both evaluations find SUPPORTED that chemically inactivated trimers still enhance activity, indicating structural rather than purely catalytic interactions.
Agreement on absence of heterotrimers (C119-C120). Both evaluations find SUPPORTED that homotrimers, not heterotrimers, are formed and isolated, challenging previous heterotrimer models.

Divergent evaluation of assembly model (C16-C17, C131-C136). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature and lack of direct structural evidence for CSR-CSR interfaces. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, viewing the homotrimer-based hexamer model as an important contribution despite raising questions.
OpenEval addresses technical observations about monomer presence and trimer stability (C44-C45, C47) from purification experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval addresses reconciliation with prior dimerization findings from Qiao et al. 2021 (C125-C126). No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval addresses contextualization with prior in vivo work (C127-C128). Peer review R14 shares C128 but focuses on the broader assembly model rather than this specific contextualization.

OpenEval explicitly identifies speculative claims about functional mechanisms and biological significance (C124, C137-C142) as UNCERTAIN, representing hypotheses for future investigation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
